Historical overturns exist but are uncommon, and Sabah-focused petitions raise only a small residual risk, yielding a low-probability overturn scenario by May 1, 2026.
summary: Lamag by-election result was BN victory with a large majority and no Lamag-specific petitions reported by Jan–Feb 2026.
Historical overturns in Malaysia are rare, with recent petition signals not targeting Lamag; Sabah petitions exist but have not overturned Lamag.
The posterior probability of an overturn before May 1, 2026 is calibrated around 1%, reflecting a conservative Bayesian update.
Nonzero risk remains due to Sabah petition activity elsewhere (Sindumin) and historical precedents, but signals for Lamag are unfavorable to overturn.

justification.synthesis_rationale: The factors were integrated by weighing the strongest signal—the confirmed Lamag result and absence of Lamag petitions—heavily downward. Sabah-specific petition activity introduces a nonzero, but weak, upward risk; the historical rarity of overturns provides a downward calibration. Correlations (e.g., Sabah petitions reflecting broader environment) are acknowledged, but the dominant, direct Lamag signals anchor the posterior near 1% with a narrow uncertainty band.

question: Will the official result of the Lamag by-election (Sabah), scheduled for January 24, 2026, be overturned before May 1, 2026?
summary: Lamag was won by BN with a large margin, which lowers the probability of overturn.
Sabah petition activity (Sindumin) shows nonzero risk, but there have been no Lamag-specific petitions reported as of early 2026.
Historical overturns exist but are relatively rare in Malaysia, suggesting a low baseline risk.
Calibration up from the ensemble due to nonzero risk signals yields a centered estimate around 4% with a plausible 2–8% range.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections identify plausible nonzero risk from Sabah petitions and historical overturns, but there is no Lamag-specific petition evidence; the risk remains low and not systemic.
justification.adjustment: Raised from 0.02 to 0.04 to reflect nonzero risk from Sabah petition activity and historical precedents, while keeping strong signals from the large BN majority and lack of Lamag petitions.

causal-factors.rationale: Past high-profile overturns exist (Kimanis 2019; Cameron Highlands 2018; Kuala Terengganu 2023), but such events are rare; GE15 petitions were rejected by the Federal Court, signaling a low historical overturn rate. ([themalaysianinsight.com](https://www.themalaysianinsight.com/s/176030?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Sindumin Sabah petition activity demonstrates nonzero risk

causal-factors.name: Sabah petition outcomes (Bersatu Sabah petitions denied) indicate low overturn likelihood
causal-factors.rationale: A Sabah-focused bid to overturn seat results was denied by the Federal Court (Jan 2026), suggesting a higher hurdle for overturn petitions in Sabah. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2025/08/04/bersatu-fails-in-appeal-to-challenge-dewan-rakyat-speaker039s-decision-on-sabah-seats?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Official Lamag result status (BN win; sworn in; no credible overturn signals)
causal-factors.rationale: Lamag was won by BN by a substantial margin; the winner was sworn in and there are no credible reports of Lamag-specific petitions, which strongly lowers overturn risk before May 1, 2026. ([theborneopost.com](https://www.theborneopost.com/2025/12/31/third-election-petition-filed/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent of overturning results due to ballot irregularities (Kimanis GE14, Sabah 2019)
causal-factors.rationale: The Kimanis GE14 case nullified the result after finding ballot irregularities, demonstrating that proven tampering or miscount can overturn results in Sabah; Lamag remains vulnerable only if similar irregularities are proven. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2019/08/16/anifah039s-kimanis-win-declared-null-and-void?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Active Sabah petition environment (Sindumin 2025; petitions filed and progressing with scheduled hearings in early 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: A Sindumin petition filed in December 2025, with a scheduled February 2026 hearing, shows that Sabah election results can be challenged procedurally and possibly overturned if irregularities are found; this raises the risk for Lamag by extension. ([malaymail.com](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2025/12/27/sabah-polls-election-petition-filed-to-annul-sindumin-seat-result-over-alleged-ballot-misconduct/203430?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Lamag by-election result with a large BN majority (5,681) relative to typical margins
causal-factors.rationale: BN’s official Lamag majority of 5,681 (7,269 vs 1,588) makes a successful overturn less probable unless substantial irregularities are demonstrated. ([malaymail.com](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/01/24/bn-retains-lamag-seat-mohd-ismail-wins-with-majority-of-5681-kinabatangan-result-still-unofficial/206706?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Judicial climate and recent Sabah-related overturn attempts (Federal Court/BERSATU Sabah rulings)
causal-factors.rationale: High-profile Sabah rulings in early 2026 (e.g., Bersatu’s bid to challenge Sabah seat rulings denied by the Federal Court) reflect a cautious judiciary less inclined to overturn election outcomes. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/01/09/apex-court-dismisses-bersatu039s-bid-to-appeal-speaker039s-decision-on-sabah-mp-seats?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Timeframe and petition-process dynamics (petition filed Dec 2025; potential timelines to May 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: petitions filed in late 2025 have to navigate court timelines; while possible, the combination of procedural hurdles and timing reduces the odds of an overturn by May 1, 2026. ([nst.com.my](https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/regional/2025/12/1344859/voter-files-petition-challenge-sindumin-seat-results?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Context of irregularity concerns in Sabah elections (Sindumin-like incidents; broader audit risk)
causal-factors.rationale: Publicized concerns about ballot handling in Sabah (e.g., Sindumin video allegations) keep the door open for petitions, even if Lamag-specific evidence is not yet public. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2025/12/27/voter-files-an-election-petition-to-annul-sindumin-results-after-video-shows-crumpled-ballot?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: No Lamag-specific election petitions reported by May 2026
causal-factors.rationale: As of late January 2026 there were no reported petitions challenging the Lamag by-election result, while Sabah petitions exist for Sindumin, suggesting any overturn would need to overcome a strong local precedent against Lamag.

causal-factors.name: Historical rarity of election-petition overturns in Malaysia
causal-factors.rationale: Past high-profile overturns (e.g., Kimanis 2019, Cameron Highlands 2018, Kuala Terengganu 2023) are uncommon, implying low odds of reversal in Lamag.

causal-factors.name: Large Lamag by-election majority in the result
causal-factors.rationale: The Lamag result delivered a sizable majority (approximately 5,681) over Warisan, reducing the incentive and likelihood for an overturn.

causal-factors.name: Active petition activity in Sabah (Sindumin) but not Lamag
causal-factors.rationale: There are Sabah petitions targeting other seats (Sindumin) which demonstrates that petition routes exist, keeping nonzero risk; however, Lamag-specific petitions have not surfaced.

causal-factors.name: Sabah/federal court rulings against overturning Sabah seat results
causal-factors.rationale: Recent court actions limiting overturn attempts in Sabah elections suggest a higher barrier to overturns generally.

synthesis: The Lamag result appears stable, but Sabah petition activity and past overturns introduce a nonzero risk. A modest upward calibration from 2% to about 4% reflects these signals while emphasizing the strong current evidence supporting the original result.
